name: source
description: Executes a script IN the current shell (no subshell), so its variable and function definitions persist afterward. Dot (.) is the POSIX synonym.

flags.description: Read and execute the file in the current shell.

examples.explanation: Applies changes you just made to .bashrc without logging out — the standard reload.
Loads shared settings (APIs, paths) from a file, then runs the deploy with them.
Activates a Python virtual environment — the most famous source use case.

about: source runs the file line by line in YOUR shell: variables, functions, cd, and umask changes persist. Executing the file normally (./script.sh) runs it in a child shell whose changes vanish — the key difference.
mistakes: Confusing source file with ./file — only the first changes your current shell.
warnings: source executes arbitrary code with your current privileges. Never source files you have not reviewed.
